title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: In A, 'f' injective' is equivalent to α_* commuting with binary intersections only because Γ is a graph, i.e. (f,f'): Γ→E×E' is injective. For a general span the condition is injectivity of f' up to f-identification. The note says 'Γ le graphe', so this is fine.
In B(ii) the correspondence is denoted β (presumably the transpose of α) without being introduced on this page. The statement is correct for β = transpose.
In Corollary 2(i) the arrows over α are written inconsistently (overline vs. arrow). This is purely notational.
Otherwise the statements check out as elementary set theory.

ideas.what: Relations/correspondences acting on power sets by f'_!f^{-1}. Lattice-theoretic characterisation of when a relation is (the inverse of) a map: preservation of ∧ / complement / 1.
ideas.modern_name: Maps in the allegory of relations (functional and total relations: R R° ≤ 1, 1 ≤ R°R). Sup-lattice maps P(E)→P(E') ≅ relations. Boolean-algebra homomorphisms P(E)→P(E') ≅ maps E'→E (discrete Stone duality).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Tarski/Lindenbaum for complete atomic Boolean algebras); allegory formulation by Freyd–Scedrov (1990); Lawvere's hyperdoctrines

ideas.what: Factorisation of a correspondence as (comorphism)∘(morphism), with injective/surjective variants characterised by preservation of 1, of disjointness, and reflection of ∅.
ideas.modern_name: Span/relation factorisation; epi–mono factorisation of relations

ideas.what: Using the set-theoretic case as a test model for the lattice-only formalism of 'ateliers'/'dispositions géminales', and noting the expected failure of the equivalences outside Boolean settings.
ideas.modern_name: Point-free (locale/frame-theoretic) correspondences; non-Boolean failure of complement-based characterisations

deep.surprise_reason: This page is an elementary, correct catalogue of how lattice properties of α_* characterise maps among relations on power sets. The material is standard (discrete Stone duality, allegories). Its only interest is as a calibration step for Grothendieck's unpublished 'ateliers' formalism.
transcription_corrections: (iv) of Corollary 1 reads 'α est un comorphisme' (not 'isomorphisme'). The insertion reads 'i.e. f': Γ ≃ E'' (not 'f: E ≃ E'').
B(iii): 'α composé d'un comorphisme, et d'un morphisme surjectif' (the transcription is roughly right).
Corollary 2(iii): 'α est composé d'un comorphisme défini par une application surjective f, et d'un morphisme injectif'.
Corollary 3(iii): 'α est un comorphisme correspondant à une application surjective g: E'→E'.
